title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Cost of Living Support and Other Measures) Bill 2022
short_title: Treasury Laws Amendment (Cost of Living Support and Other Measures) Bill 2022

divisions.question: The majority voted in favour of a [motion](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2022-03-30.194.1) to keep unchanged table item 2.2.55 of item (1) and item (8) of schedule 3. In parliamentary jargon, they voted that the items "*stand as printed*." This vote took place after NSW Senator [Mehreen Faruqi](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/nsw/mehreen_faruqi) (Greens) proposed that they be opposed. Because this vote was successful, the items will remain as they are. ### What did these items do? [According to Senator Faruqi](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?id=2022-03-30.194.1): > *... here we have a government trying to sneak in deductible gift status for the [Ramsay Centre for Western Civilisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Ramsay#Ramsay_Centre_for_Western_Civilisation), a move that will allow the centre to avoid taxation on their income. My amendment will stop this from happening.* But Victorian Senator [Jane Hume](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/senate/victoria/jane_hume) (Liberal) disagreed, [saying](https://www.openaustralia.org.au/senate/?gid=2022-03-30.195.1): > *I think the senator has misunderstood what DGR status actually implies. It does not mean that the Ramsay centre doesn't pay tax; it means that donors to the Ramsay centre are allowed to deduct their donations.*

speeches.speaker: Paul Fletcher
speeches.brief: The speaker moved to suspend standing orders to rescind the resolution fixing debate on the Treasury Laws Amendment (Cost of Living Support and Other Measures) Bill 2022 for the next sitting and to adjourn the debate to a later hour this day.

speeches.speaker: David Coleman
speeches.brief: The Morrison government announced a one-off cost-of-living tax offset of up to $1,500 for single-income and $3,000 for dual-income households for the 2021-22 income year, benefiting over 10 million taxpayers, and a six-month fuel excise reduction from 30 March to 28 September 2022.
